subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Transfer Costs
description: A short lesson to help you apply Data Transfer Costs.

hook.text: Uploading data to the cloud is free. Downloading it will cost you. Welcome to egress charges.

buildup.text: Cloud providers charge for data leaving their network. The more you download, the higher the bill.

discovery.text: AWS charges up to $0.09 per gigabyte for data transfer out. At scale, that adds up to millions.

twist.text: This creates lock-in. Moving your data to another provider means paying massive egress fees to leave.

climax.text: Google and Cloudflare challenged this by cutting egress fees. The industry is slowly changing.

punchline.text: Getting data in is free. Getting it out costs you.

quiz.question: Why do egress charges create cloud lock-in?
options: Moving data to another provider requires paying expensive transfer-out fees
Egress charges make it illegal to switch cloud providers
Data can only be downloaded once from any cloud service

details.summary: Data transfer costs charge for moving data between cloud regions, availability zones, services, and to the internet. Ingress is usually free but egress can cost $0.09 per gigabyte or more. At petabyte scale, data transfer bills can exceed compute costs.
details.whyItMatters: Data transfer is the most underestimated cost in cloud architectures. Poor placement of services across zones and regions can generate massive unexpected transfer charges.
takeaways: Ingress is typically free; egress incurs per-gigabyte charges
Cross-region and cross-AZ transfer adds considerable cost
Architecture decisions directly impact transfer bills

faq.question: How can you reduce data transfer costs?
faq.answer: Colocate communicating services in the same availability zone. Use VPC endpoints to avoid NAT gateway charges. Compress data before transfer. Use CDNs for outbound traffic to users. Consider providers with free egress for bandwidth-heavy workloads.

faq.question: Which cloud providers have the cheapest data transfer?
faq.answer: Cloudflare offers free egress on its R2 storage. Oracle Cloud includes generous free egress. GCP and Azure are generally cheaper than AWS for egress. AWS charges the most for data transfer but has the largest ecosystem. Competition is driving prices down.
